title: fix(desktop): tag registry imports once and is never overwritten when untrusted (audit LIB-A4, LIB-B6, LIB-B7)
body:
## What was broken

- LIB-A4 / LIB-B7: with no `tags.json`, every `tags:list` re-ran the legacy Phase 1 tag import (a full vault scan), because the registry was only written when legacy tags existed. `list()` also scanned the vault for counts even with zero tags.
- LIB-B6: any read error or parse failure of `tags.json` (corrupt JSON, newer version, EIO/EACCES) was treated as "no registry", so the next tag write replaced the file and erased every tag.

## What changed (`src/main/library/tag-repository.ts` + tests)

- `importLegacy` always persists the registry (even empty) before rewriting sidecars, so the import runs exactly once per vault.
- `list()` returns `[]` without scanning when there are no live tags.
- `read()`: only ENOENT means "no registry". Corrupt/newer-version JSON throws `TagRegistryError("corrupt")` after copying the file to `tags.json.corrupt-<ts>` once per session; other read errors throw `TagRegistryError("unreadable")`. All write paths call `read()` first, so writes are refused and the file is untouched.

Behaviour change: a corrupt `tags.json` now makes `tags:list` reject (the existing `errorTags` toast) instead of silently showing no tags and later wiping the file. Follow-up outside this PR: `use-tags.ts` `create` calls `listTags()` unguarded in its catch block, so with a corrupt registry `create` rejects instead of returning `null`.

## How it was verified

From `apps/kaipu-record`:
- `bun run test src/main/library/tag-repository.test.ts`: 21 passed (6 new).
- `bun run check-types`: no errors.
- `bun run lint`: 0 errors (17 pre-existing warnings).
- Full `bun run test`: 2178 tests passed; 3 files (`library-service`, `edit-project-probe`, `video-edit-session`) fail to load only because Electron's binary is not installed in this worktree (`bun install --ignore-scripts`); unrelated to this change.

Note: the new "writes the registry before stripping legacy tags" test uses a persistent `writeMeta` rejection, since `vault.list()` now backfills identity via `writeMeta` and swallows its errors (would consume a one-shot mock).

## Findings closed

LIB-A4, LIB-B7, LIB-B6. The plan lives in PR #301 (`docs/code-audit-2026-10-15`, `plans/audit-2026-10-15/07-tags-registry-integrity.md`); it is not on main, so this PR does not delete it.

## How to test it yourself

1. Open the Library on a vault that never had tags: `<vault>/.kaipu/tags.json` appears as `{"version":1,"tags":[]}` and stays across reopenings.
2. Quit, edit `tags.json` to `{bad`, reopen: tags toast appears, creating a tag fails, the file is unchanged and one `tags.json.corrupt-<ts>` sits beside it.
3. Restore a valid file: tags work again.
